title: 1.4.0 - Release Notes
excerpt: Release notes for Ghostty 1.4.0, released on October 27, 2026.
content_html:
Ghostty 1.4.0 is a major release that includes large performance and memory improvements, a 100% complete Kitty graphics implementation including animation and relative placements (the first non-Kitty terminal to do so), SSH integration improvements, and hundreds more improvements and fixes across all platforms.

This release features 7 months of work with changes from 172 contributors over 2,889 commits. Thank you to all the contributors, maintainers, community moderators, translators, packagers, and users who each helped make this release possible.

These release notes are painstakingly and lovingly hand-crafted by human Ghostty maintainers, including the full changelog. They take a combined 16+ hours to write, so please enjoy. 🥰

  • GHSA-4hwh-wx3w-3fqg. Paste protection didn't treat carriage returns as line endings, so a paste could run a command without confirmation in programs that don't use bracketed paste. This requires user interaction (copy-paste) to trigger.
  • GHSA-mhff-mv4q-fp63. Malicious Kitty graphics commands could crash or hang Ghostty, force huge allocations, or in limited cases read or delete files outside the allowed temporary directories. This only requires displaying malicious output.
  • GHSA-hcr9-7hcr-mjm8. Malicious terminal output could crash Ghostty, closing every window, via tmux control mode. tmux doesn't need to be installed. This affects Ghostty 1.3.0 and 1.3.1.
  • GHSA-hp9c-qp4q-cpw3. The same impact as above, via a tmux control mode layout with a zero-sized or oversized pane. This affects Ghostty 1.3.0 and 1.3.1.
  • GHSA-w9q4-5jvv-mcv4. Clearing the screen into scrollback could corrupt memory if it deleted the scrollback page holding a styled or hyperlinked cursor. This only requires displaying malicious output, but only with a small scrollback-limit such as 0. The default isn't known to be affected.
  • GHSA-2r63-vmw6-3m3c. A crafted directory name could make the zsh shell integration send arbitrary escape sequences, such as silently replacing the clipboard via OSC 52. bash was affected in a more limited way. This only requires cd-ing into a directory from untrusted content, such as a cloned repository.
  • macOS: GHSA-cw69-wm67-5pv8. Cmd-clicking a crafted OSC 8 hyperlink could open unsafe local files or custom URL schemes, leading to arbitrary command execution. Ghostty now blocks unsafe targets and confirms custom URL schemes. This requires user interaction (cmd-click) to trigger.
  • macOS: GHSA-mfw9-xcr3-7gfp. The same issue as above for links detected by the link configuration, including the default URL matcher. This requires user interaction (cmd-click) to trigger.
  • macOS: GHSA-v8cw-fg4j-jcc4. Drag-and-drop text skipped paste protection, with the same impact as above. This requires user interaction (drag-and-drop) to trigger.
  • macOS: GHSA-mxqx-236q-wrv7. Opening a file whose name contains control characters could run a different command than the one shown in the confirmation dialog. This requires a crafted file on your system and confirming the dialog.

Note: I requested CVEs for the above advisories weeks ago, but GitHub hasn't assigned them yet. If/when they're assigned, I will update the above with proper CVE numbers.

PRs: #12999 #13069 #13393 #14413 #14414

Ghostty 1.4 supports macOS 27 (Golden Gate). Most of the work was compatibility fixes:

  • Tabs in the titlebar (macos-titlebar-style = tabs) lay out correctly again.
  • The native tab bar no longer draws as a solid gray bar on top of your theme. It now lets the new glass style blend with your terminal background.
  • macos-titlebar-style = hidden no longer covers the top lines of the terminal when Reduce Transparency is on.
  • The app icon no longer has a thin border.
  • The Shortcuts "New Window" action no longer opens two windows when Ghostty is running without any windows.

Ghostty 1.4 remains fully compatible with prior macOS versions back to and including macOS 13 (Ventura). See the system requirements for more details.

Ghostty 1.3.1 works on macOS 27, but it has some of the visual issues listed above, such as the gray tab bar.

PRs: #13943 #13939 #13935 #13934 #13893 #13933 #13389 #13270 #13281

Ghostty now supports Kitty graphics animation and relative placements. These were the last major features of the Kitty graphics protocol that Ghostty didn't support.

Programs that display animated images with the Kitty protocol, such as an animated GIF shown with kitten icat, now animate in Ghostty instead of showing a single still frame. Frame transmission, composition, and playback control are all supported, and animations pause while the terminal isn't visible. Relative placements let a program position one image relative to another image's placement, so the child image moves along with its parent.

We also did a full conformance pass against the specification and Kitty itself, fixing dozens of behavioral differences. For example, images now scroll with text inside scroll regions (#4323 ), retransmitting an image ID replaces the old image (#6711 ), and invalid image data now gets an error response instead of silence, which could leave clients hanging. The full list is in the terminal capabilities section.

Kitty graphics are faster, too. Image payloads are now parsed in bulk with SIMD instead of one byte at a time, making large image transfers about 16x faster to parse in our benchmarks (64 MiB of image data, x86_64 Linux), and drawing images costs much less per frame.

Our Kitty graphics implementation now covers 100% of the published specification, making Ghostty (and libghostty) the first terminal to do this outside of Kitty itself.

PRs: #13264 #13473 #13240 #13245 #14130 #14137 #14138 #14017

Ghostty now transparently compresses scrollback that isn't visible, reducing the physical memory those pages use by 70% to 90% for typical text-heavy history. Compression only runs while the terminal is idle and pages are decompressed on demand when you scroll back or search, so it has no measurable impact on I/O throughput.

Thanks to compression, the default scrollback limit has been raised from 10 MB to 50 MB per terminal. On platforms that support compression, a full scrollback still generally uses less physical memory than the old 10 MB limit did.

Compression lowers resident (physical) memory, not virtual memory, so look at resident memory when measuring it. It is currently available on macOS and 64-bit Linux.

Beyond scrollback, memory usage is lower in many places:

  • A new, empty terminal now uses about 16 KiB of terminal page memory on macOS, down from 128 KiB in Ghostty 1.3.1.
  • On macOS and Linux, memory freed by clearing or trimming scrollback is now returned to the OS instead of being held until the terminal closes.
  • Hidden tabs release their GPU resources. On macOS, with one visible tab and 20 hidden tabs, GPU memory dropped from about 385 MiB to 18 MiB. Rebuilding them when a tab becomes visible again takes under a millisecond.

PRs: #13209 #13220 #13226 #13227 #13537 #13827 #13587 #14011 #13722 #14035 #12760

There are performance improvements across the board in Ghostty 1.4 that yield significant gains compared to prior Ghostty versions.

The biggest win came from a surprising discovery: on macOS, the kernel caps every read from a pty at about 1 KiB no matter how large the read buffer is. Previously, Ghostty processed each read as it arrived, so per-read overhead was paid every kilobyte, and the program writing output sat blocked while we parsed. Ghostty now drains the pty on one thread while parsing on another, raising end-to-end I/O throughput by 25% to 55% on macOS (M4 Max, plain and Unicode text) over Ghostty 1.3.x.

VT processing itself is also much faster. In parser benchmarks, plain ASCII text went from 128 MB/s to 725 MB/s (5.7x), CJK text got 3.4x faster, and a 2.6 GB dataset of real-world terminal recordings from asciinema is processed about 25% faster. Together, these changes took cat-ing a 150 MB text file on macOS from 1.5 seconds to 566 milliseconds.

Other notable improvements:

  • Resize: resizing a terminal with a large scrollback is about 6x faster (120x80 with 10,000 lines of scrollback), and 3x to 5x faster with history full of CJK text or emoji.
  • Rendering: the renderer holds the terminal lock 2.7x to 11x less per frame, leaving more time for the I/O thread during heavy output.
  • Copy and search: formatting terminal contents as plain text, HTML, or VT, which backs clipboard copy, write_screen_file, and scrollback search, is 1.5x to 8x faster.
  • Launch (macOS): about 15% faster from launch to visible window, and 27% faster to the first rendered frame.
  • Idle energy: on macOS, the renderer's display link now sleeps when there's nothing to draw. On GTK, hidden tabs stop rendering, matching macOS.
  • Large OSC sequences: OSC 52 clipboard payloads parse about 30x faster, and even short sequences like title changes are about 6x faster.

PRs: #14052 #14269

The GTK app has a new rendering pipeline. It no longer uses GtkGLArea. Instead, the renderer draws with EGL on its own thread, exports each frame as a DMABUF, and hands it to GTK to display. Rendering is now triple-buffered, which should greatly reduce tearing, and no OpenGL calls run on the main thread anymore, which let us remove a number of workarounds.

The most visible result is crisp text under fractional scaling. Text and box-drawing characters are no longer blurry with fractional display scaling such as 125% or 150% (#1938 ). We fixed this once before, but it came back after upstream GTK changes. Ghostty now renders at the window's true fractional scale, so every rendered pixel maps to exactly one pixel on screen.

The new render surface needs a system EGL library (see Changes for Package Maintainers). On GPU drivers that can't export DMABUFs, Ghostty falls back to copying frames through the CPU, which is slower but works.

PRs: #13962 #13993 #13995 #13998 #14002 #14061

Ghostty now implements the Kitty clipboard protocol (OSC 5522) on both macOS and GTK. Ghostty 1.3 could parse the protocol but didn't implement it.

OSC 52 can only read and write plain text. The Kitty clipboard protocol lets programs running in the terminal read and write any kind of clipboard data, such as images or HTML, and lets them pick among the formats on the clipboard. Programs can also enable paste events (mode 5522), which tell the program what formats a paste contains so it can read the one it wants. This is how a terminal program can accept a pasted image, for example.

Clipboard access follows the existing clipboard-read and clipboard-write configurations. By default, reads prompt for permission and writes are allowed. The permission prompt shows a preview of the clipboard contents, including images. Programs that send a password can have your answer remembered for the rest of that terminal session. A new clipboard-write-limit-bytes configuration limits the size of a single write (default 64 MiB). A write over the limit fails and leaves the clipboard untouched.

PRs: #10423 #13706

You can now rearrange splits on GTK by dragging them, matching the macOS feature introduced in Ghostty 1.3. When a tab has two or more splits, each split shows a drag handle at the top. Grab the handle and drop the split onto any other split, including splits in other tabs and windows. An overlay shows which side of the target split it will land on. The terminal contents, working directory, and running processes all move with it.

A new drag-handle configuration controls when drag handles are shown on both macOS and GTK: auto (default), always, or never. With never, splits can't be rearranged with the mouse. Hiding the handles was a common request from users who found them in the way.

On GTK, splits can only be dropped onto other splits. Dragging a split out to create a new tab or window is macOS-only.

PRs: #14454 #13494 #14483 #14538 #14673 #14375 #14144

Ghostty 1.4 includes dozens of improvements to core terminal emulation. We now run esctest, Thomas Dickey's terminal conformance suite, against Ghostty's terminal core in CI. Alongside that, we fixed many differences from xterm in cursor movement within margins, tab stops, character sets, mode reports, and more. You can find the full list of related changes in the terminal capabilities section.

Ghostty also supports several new sequences, including soft terminal reset (DECSTR), extended cursor position reports (DECXCPR), backarrow key mode (DECBKM), and screen size reports in characters (CSI 19 t). Programs can also now ask whether the terminal is visible using visibility reports (mode 2033), so they can stop rendering while hidden.

Keyboard encoding also matches xterm more closely, with fixes for modifyOtherKeys mode 2 and legacy Alt-as-Escape encoding of non-ASCII keys.

Two new sequences are disabled by default because they can be abused by untrusted programs, including ones running on a remote machine:

# Allow programs to resize the window (CSI 8 t)
vt-window-resize-allowed = true

# Allow programs to request screen checksums (DECRQCRA)
vt-xt-checksum-report = true

PRs: #12582 #12814 #13533 #13844 #14472 #14854

Ghostty 1.2 introduced SSH shell integration features as a work in progress. In Ghostty 1.4, they're backed by a new ghostty +ssh CLI action: a drop-in ssh wrapper that prepares the remote session for Ghostty and then runs the real ssh with your arguments forwarded unchanged.

ghostty +ssh user@example.com

# Or alias it so every ssh invocation goes through it
alias ssh='ghostty +ssh --'

Before connecting, +ssh installs Ghostty's terminfo on the remote host so the proper xterm-ghostty TERM value can be used, and forwards COLORTERM, TERM_PROGRAM, and TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION. If the terminfo install fails (for example, tic isn't available on the remote), it falls back to TERM=xterm-256color. Flags such as --terminfo=false, --forward-env=false, and --verbose control each step.

The ssh-env and ssh-terminfo shell integration features (still opt-in) now call +ssh too. Previously, each shell integration carried its own copy of this logic, which made up roughly a third of our shell integration scripts. Now bash, zsh, fish, elvish, and Nushell all behave identically, and you can get the same behavior from scripts or anywhere else by calling ghostty +ssh directly.

The terminfo install itself is also more reliable. Ghostty now always installs its own bundled terminfo rather than accepting whatever xterm-ghostty entry the remote already has, and it reinstalls automatically when a Ghostty update changes the terminfo. It also no longer needs infocmp or Ghostty's terminfo on the local machine. Installs are cached per host and port, so two machines behind one address no longer share a cache entry. And ssh-env no longer silently overrides SetEnv entries in your ~/.ssh/config (#11518 ).

The +ssh-cache command that manages this cache now takes positional destinations (ghostty +ssh-cache user@example.com) and has a new --prune=30d flag. See the breaking changes if you script against +ssh-cache.

macOS: The minimum required macOS version for Ghostty 1.4 remains unchanged (macOS 13 Ventura). Ghostty is now compatible with macOS 27.

GTK: Ghostty 1.4 requires GTK 4.18 and libadwaita 1.7, up from GTK 4.14 and libadwaita 1.5 in Ghostty 1.3. This aligns with our GTK/Adwaita version policy. Notably, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS doesn't meet this requirement. Systems with older GTK or Adwaita versions can work around this requirement by using an older version of Ghostty or the Flatpak package. #14330

OpenGL (GTK): The minimum required OpenGL version remains 4.3, but Ghostty now renders through EGL instead of GTK's OpenGL widget. This should be invisible for nearly everyone, but if Ghostty fails to start with an EGL error, please make sure your GPU driver provides a working EGL implementation.

We previously announced that Ghostty 1.4 would require macOS 14. Nothing forced our hand to do this in this release, so we kept macOS 13 support. We still plan to drop macOS 13 in a future release. Apple dropped security support for macOS 13 in the fall of 2025, so we recommend upgrading regardless.

The following behaviors have changed in 1.4.0:

  • copy-on-select has been reworked and now accepts none, primary, clipboard, or both. The meaning of clipboard has changed: it previously copied to both the selection clipboard and the system clipboard, and now copies only to the system clipboard. If you set copy-on-select = clipboard and want the old behavior, change it to both. #12600 #12604
  • macOS: copy-on-select now defaults to none (previously true), so selecting text no longer copies it anywhere and middle-click paste of the selection no longer works by default. To restore the 1.3 behavior, set copy-on-select = primary. Note that an explicit copy-on-select = true on macOS now copies selections to the system clipboard, which is different from 1.3. #12600 #12604
  • macOS: cmd+arrow_up and cmd+arrow_down now run jump_to_prompt again, matching Terminal.app and Ghostty 1.2. In 1.3, these keys were hardcoded to scroll to the top and bottom and couldn't be rebound. To keep the 1.3 behavior, set keybind = cmd+arrow_up=scroll_to_top and keybind = cmd+arrow_down=scroll_to_bottom. #12245
  • GTK: The default ctrl+shift+page_up and ctrl+shift+page_down keybinds now move the current tab left and right (move_tab), matching Firefox, GNOME Terminal, and VS Code. jump_to_prompt moved to ctrl+shift+arrow_up and ctrl+shift+arrow_down, so programs running in the terminal no longer receive those keys. If a program you use needs them, unbind them with keybind = ctrl+shift+arrow_up=unbind and keybind = ctrl+shift+arrow_down=unbind. #4998 #12458

The list below contains deprecations that remain compatible today through a compatibility layer, but may break in a future release if they are ignored:

  • scrollback-limit has been renamed to scrollback-limit-bytes, to make room for the new scrollback-limit-lines. #13473
  • copy-on-select = true is replaced with copy-on-select = primary on Linux and FreeBSD, or copy-on-select = clipboard on macOS. copy-on-select = false is replaced with copy-on-select = none. #12600 #12604

There is no set timeline to remove these deprecations, but we recommend adapting to the new configurations sooner rather than later to avoid any possible disruptions in the future.

  • Scrollback history is now transparently compressed while the terminal is idle, reducing the physical memory used by compressed scrollback by 70% to 90% for typical text. Compression is available on macOS and 64-bit Linux and can be disabled with the new scrollback-compression configuration. Because of this, the default scrollback limit has been raised from 10 MB to 50 MB, which on average still uses less memory than a full scrollback did previously. #13264
  • A new configuration scrollback-limit-lines limits scrollback by number of lines instead of bytes. The existing scrollback-limit configuration has been renamed to scrollback-limit-bytes (the old name continues to work). If both are set, the first limit reached applies, and both accept unlimited. #13473
  • copy-on-select now accepts none, primary, clipboard, and both and no longer affects middle-click paste (see middle-click-action). clipboard now copies only to the system clipboard, so use both for the previous behavior. The default on macOS is now none. See the breaking changes for migration details. #12600
  • A new configuration middle-click-action configures the behavior of middle-clicking: primary-paste (default) pastes from the selection clipboard, clipboard-paste pastes from the system clipboard, and ignore does nothing. #12478
  • A new binding action move_tab_to_new_window moves the current tab into a new window of its own. It is also available in the command palette. #2630
  • A new CLI command +explain-config prints the documentation for a configuration option or binding action, e.g. ghostty +explain-config font-size. #11546
  • The +explain-config and +show-config CLI commands now page their output through $GHOSTTY_PAGER or $PAGER (falling back to less) when run interactively. Paging can be disabled with --no-pager or by setting the pager to an empty value. #11940
  • A new configuration drag-handle controls when the split drag handles are shown: auto (default), always, or never. #13706 #13709
  • Scrollback search now wraps around when navigating past the first or last match. #11449
  • A new configuration link-osc8 (default true) can be set to false to disable OSC 8 hyperlinks entirely. Disabled OSC 8 hyperlinks are not highlighted, previewed, copied, or opened. #13634
  • Processes running in Ghostty now receive a GHOSTTY_SURFACE_ID environment variable that uniquely identifies the terminal they are running in. #12027
  • The right-click context menu now has a "Close Split" item. #11173 #11174
  • Upgrade to Unicode 18. #14293
  • I/O throughput is 25% to 55% higher on macOS by reading from the pty concurrently with parsing previously read output. #13209
  • VT processing is significantly faster across the board. Plain text is up to ~6x faster, real-world output (measured against a large asciinema dataset) is ~24% faster, grapheme-heavy output is ~3x faster, and DEC special graphics (line drawing), repeated characters (REP), hyperlink-heavy output, and scroll regions are all faster. #13220 #13226 #13231 #13294 #13625 #13826 #14356
  • Large OSC sequences, such as OSC 52 clipboard writes, are parsed ~30x faster and small OSC sequences, such as title changes, ~6x faster. #14011 #13565
  • Resizing with reflow is ~6x faster with large scrollback and 3x to 5x faster with scrollback heavy in wide characters such as CJK or emoji. #13537 #13827
  • Terminals use significantly less memory. A new terminal now uses ~16 KiB of physical memory for its screen instead of 128 KiB on macOS, every terminal page uses 30% less memory, and memory freed from scrollback (such as by clearing it) is now returned to the operating system. #13240 #13245 #14130 #14137 #14138
  • Kitty graphics are faster. Large image transfers are parsed in bulk using SIMD, zlib-compressed images decompress ~17% faster, pixel format conversion avoids an extra copy, and the per-frame cost of drawing images is much lower, especially with Unicode placeholder images on screen or long scrollback. #13270 #13281 #13987 #14422 #14780 #14789
  • Formatting terminal contents is 1.5x to 8x faster, which speeds up clipboard copy (plain, HTML, and VT), write_screen_file and related actions, and scrollback search. #13587
  • The renderer holds the terminal lock 2.7x to 11x less time per frame, and glyph and font lookups are faster. #13227 #14300 #14301 #14420 #14406 #13258
  • command-palette-entry = clear removes all command palette entries, including the default entries. #12682
  • window-padding-balance has a new value equal that balances padding equally on all four sides without capping the top padding. #11491
  • theme now expands ~ to the home directory in theme file paths, including in separate light and dark themes. #13840
  • +list-themes now supports g and G to jump to the first and last theme, and ctrl+d and ctrl+u to page down and up. #13681 #14607
  • The terminal inspector can now copy terminal I/O events or export them to a file. #13519
  • Bundled themes updated to release-20261019-151001-86a776d. This adds 356 new themes and renames or removes none. The colors of 10 existing themes changed upstream: Adwaita, Adwaita Dark, Atom One Light, Catppuccin Frappe, Catppuccin Latte, Catppuccin Macchiato, Catppuccin Mocha, Cursor Dark, Dark Modern, and Electron Highlighter.
  • Fix configuration parsing silently ignoring all settings after a comment or blank line that happened to end at an internal buffer boundary. This typically only affected long configuration files. #13638
  • Fix a performance degradation where, after a long uptime, the renderer rebuilt its full terminal state on every frame. #13585
  • Fix the automatically created configuration file being empty instead of containing the configuration template. #13774
  • +edit-config works when $EDITOR or $VISUAL contains arguments, such as zed --new. #11897
  • adjust-cursor-height works again. #13225
  • Mouse selection improvements: dragging after a ctrl/cmd triple-click output selection now extends the selection by command output, autoscroll stops when the screen switches (e.g. to the alternate screen), a force touch on macOS selects the word at the press location without starting a drag, and releasing a drag no longer activates a link or prompt click. #12830
  • Double-click word selection no longer continues across hard line breaks, and double-clicking either half of a wide character (such as CJK) selects the whole word. #14354 #14391
  • Wide characters at the edges of a selection are now consistently rendered as selected and included when copying, including when the wide character wraps onto a new internal page. #14632 #14651
  • Triple-click line selection no longer pulls in neighboring prompt text when clicking blank cells between OSC 133 prompt boundaries. #14553
  • Link detection and double-click selection no longer merge prompt text with the command text next to it when shell integration is active. #12435
  • File paths opened with cmd/ctrl-click no longer include trailing spaces, which broke opening paths printed by some TUIs. #13505
  • Mouse releases are now reported to the program that received the mouse press when clicking at a shell prompt with click-to-move enabled. This fixes double-click selection in programs like fzf's ctrl+r history search. #14710
  • Shell redraws after a resize are no longer processed at the old terminal size. This fixes one cause of duplicated or misplaced prompts after resizing. #14706
  • Scrolling, such as clicking in the scrollbar, now works with very large scrollback (millions of lines). #13048
  • Custom command-palette-entry actions with string parameters, such as set_tab_title, no longer have their parameters escaped when run from the command palette. #13609
  • HTML clipboard copies no longer include a superfluous trailing newline. #13543
  • Copying as VT (copy_to_clipboard:vt) and VT screen files now preserve OSC 8 hyperlinks, empty gaps between text, and cells that only have a background color, such as colored status bars. VT screen files also keep trailing blank rows. #14711 #14725 #14766
  • The mouse pointer now restores the shape set by the running program (OSC 22) after releasing modifier keys instead of resetting to the default. #14128
  • Custom shaders no longer receive swapped selection foreground and background color uniforms. #14460
  • Ghostty no longer floods the logs with "adjusting page capacity" messages during output with many styles, graphemes, or hyperlinks. #14631
  • Fix stale wrap and prompt state on rows reused after scrolling or erasing, which could cause incorrect copy, search, selection, and reflow results. #14010
  • Fix stale rendering of the previous row after erasing or deleting a wrapped wide character. #14054
  • Fix a freeze when reloading the configuration while a program is flooding the terminal with queries, such as color queries. #14833
  • +list-themes no longer crashes on some keys when the search matches no themes, and the keypad down key now moves one row instead of 21. #14612 #14605
  • Fix crashes in scrollback search after clearing the scrollback, resizing, or erasing history. #11957 #13274 #13282
  • Fix crashes and viewport corruption when resizing with scrolled-back history or with the cursor near the bottom of the screen. #12300 #12907 #12935
  • Fix a use-after-free crash when clicking or selecting text during heavy output. #12463
  • Fix a possible crash when reflowing hyperlinks during a resize. #13524
  • Fix possible crashes or memory corruption when scrolling or erasing rows across a page boundary that needed more capacity. #13394 #13397
  • Fix possible crashes and memory corruption found via fuzzing when printing causes a page to grow, or after clearing the screen into scrollback. #11261 #13997
  • Fix many latent crashes and undefined behavior in selection, pins, search, title and working directory updates, and resize error handling. #12894 #13275 #13278 #13367
  • Fix a possible crash or corrupted input when many pty writes are queued, such as during large pastes. #13659
  • Fix an out-of-bounds access when IME preedit text with wide characters is composed between existing wide characters, such as with Korean input. #12479
  • Fix a crash when pressing or releasing mouse button 11. #14759
  • Fix the write_screen_file, write_scrollback_file, and write_selection_file actions leaking two file descriptors on each use, which could eventually prevent opening new terminals. #13644
  • Fix memory and file descriptor leaks in terminal I/O, including for writes in read-only mode and files read via the input configuration. #13574 #13579 #13931
  • vt: Kitty graphics animation is now fully supported: frame transmission, composition, animation control, and rendering. #5255 #13943
  • vt: Kitty graphics relative placements (P=, Q=, H=, V=) are now supported, allowing images to be positioned relative to other images. #13939
  • vt: Support the Kitty graphics transient image usage hint. Transient images are evicted first when image storage is full. #13389
  • vt: The Kitty clipboard protocol (OSC 5522) is now implemented on macOS and GTK, including paste events (mode 5522). Reads and writes follow clipboard-read and clipboard-write, and a new clipboard-write-limit-bytes configuration limits the size of a single write. #10549 #13962 #13993 #13995 #13998 #14002 #14061
  • vt: Support visibility reports (mode 2033 and CSI ? 998 n), which tell programs when the terminal is not visible, such as in a background tab or on another workspace, so they can stop rendering. #13494
  • vt: Programs can resize the window with the xterm CSI 8 ; rows ; cols t sequence if the new vt-window-resize-allowed configuration is enabled (default off). The request is ignored in splits, windows with multiple tabs, the quick terminal, and fullscreen, maximized, or tiled windows. #1115 #14375
  • vt: Support OSC 133 click_events=2, which reports prompt clicks with row coordinates relative to the prompt. #10865 #12953
  • vt: Support soft terminal reset (DECSTR, CSI ! p), which resets modes, margins, and text attributes without clearing the screen. #14538
  • vt: Support backarrow key mode (DECBKM, mode 67), which lets programs choose whether backspace sends DEL (0x7f, the default) or BS (0x08). #12226
  • vt: Support the DECRQCRA and XTCHECKSUM screen checksum reports, which are mostly used by terminal test suites. Because a program can use these to read the screen contents, they are disabled unless the new vt-xt-checksum-report configuration is enabled. The new vt-xt-checksum-extension configuration controls how the checksum is calculated. #14483
  • vt: Respond to CSI 19 t (report screen size in characters) and to DECXCPR (CSI ? 6 n) extended cursor position requests. #14633 #14673

As with 1.3, libghostty isn't directly part of the Ghostty 1.4 release. But a large part of the 1.4 development cycle went into libghostty, so here's an update.

Over the past 6 months, the C API for libghostty-vt has grown from a parser and a few encoders into a complete terminal emulator API, adopted by dozens of free and commercial terminal emulators used by millions of people. It's hard to quantify exactly, but the number of people using a libghostty-based terminal is confidently several times the number of people using the Ghostty GUI.

libghostty-vt now builds for macOS, Linux, Windows (MSVC and GNU), FreeBSD, Android, iOS, and WebAssembly, and CI continuously verifies every one of these targets. The goal is for libghostty-vt to be generally usable everywhere, within reason, so if you want more target support, let us know!

It's also easier to integrate libghostty-vt into existing build systems. There's CMake support, Nix packaging, an xcframework, and a source tarball, in addition to the existing pkg-config file. libghostty-vt no longer needs libc++, and it can build freestanding.

The API is still marked as a work in progress and broke compatibility several times during this cycle, so expect more breaking changes before a tagged release. The API documentation and the Zig, C, C++, Swift, and WebAssembly examples (now over 30) are kept up to date with main.

We're going to do a final pass over the C API, break ABI one more time, and then likely tag a libghostty 1.0 release very soon.

Ghostty is a non-profit project, fiscally sponsored by Hack Club. All of our finances are public on HCB, so you can see exactly where every dollar goes.

During the 1.4 cycle, we paid $41,820 to contributors under contract and spent about $1,260 on infrastructure such as website hosting.

I'm happy to share that we've now signed our first two 12-month contracts, which give contributors stable, long-term paid work on Ghostty and help ensure the ongoing stability and sustainability of the project:

  • @trag1c is Ghostty's head of operations. He manages the community on GitHub and Discord, coordinates our volunteer translators, and maintains various other important project systems.
  • @vancluever works on various Ghostty subsystems. In this cycle, he led the upgrade to Zig 0.16, moved the build off Zig's deprecated @cImport, updated the bundled Fontconfig, and more. He's also the author of z2d, the 2D graphics library Ghostty uses to draw box-drawing characters and other sprite glyphs.

If you'd like to support Ghostty, please visit our sponsorship page.

The primary focus of the roadmap continues to be libghostty functionality, stability, and portability. During the last release cycle, I said I aimed to tag a libghostty release. We haven't done that yet, but I'm confident we will do so before Ghostty 1.5.

libghostty is a project that continues to be the tide that lifts all boats. libghostty improvements tie directly to Ghostty GUI improvements as well as dozens of other large projects in the ecosystem. As more large projects adopt libghostty, libghostty tends to get more testing and attention, and this creates a cycle that yields the most gain for terminal emulators everywhere.

macOS and GTK builds of Ghostty have talented, capable maintainer teams that are continuing to improve them, so they're not neglected by any means! As a project, we've decided to drop any roadmap for Windows support in the Ghostty GUI. libghostty fully supports Windows (and we test it in CI), and the official stance now is that downstream projects should use that.

Our release cycle remains 6 months. This release was delayed by one month, but Ghostty 1.5 is planned for March 2027. libghostty will have a separate release cycle.
content_text: Ghostty 1.4.0 is a major release that includes large performance and memory improvements, a 100% complete Kitty graphics implementation including animation and relative placements (the first non-Kitty terminal to do so), SSH integration improvements, and hundreds more improvements and fixes across all platforms. This release features 7 months of work with changes from 172 contributors over 2,889 commits. Thank you to all the contributors, maintainers, community moderators, translators, packagers, and users who each helped make this release possible. These release notes are painstakingly and lovingly hand-crafted by human Ghostty maintainers, including the full changelog. They take a combined 16+ hours to write, so please enjoy. 🥰 GHSA-4hwh-wx3w-3fqg. Paste protection didn't treat carriage returns as line endings, so a paste could run a command without confirmation in programs that don't use bracketed paste. This requires user interaction (copy-paste) to trigger. GHSA-mhff-mv4q-fp63. Malicious Kitty graphics commands could crash or hang Ghostty, force huge allocations, or in limited cases read or delete files outside the allowed temporary directories. This only requires displaying malicious output. GHSA-hcr9-7hcr-mjm8. Malicious terminal output could crash Ghostty, closing every window, via tmux control mode. tmux doesn't need to be installed. This affects Ghostty 1.3.0 and 1.3.1. GHSA-hp9c-qp4q-cpw3. The same impact as above, via a tmux control mode layout with a zero-sized or oversized pane. This affects Ghostty 1.3.0 and 1.3.1. GHSA-w9q4-5jvv-mcv4. Clearing the screen into scrollback could corrupt memory if it deleted the scrollback page holding a styled or hyperlinked cursor. This only requires displaying malicious output, but only with a small scrollback-limit such as 0. The default isn't known to be affected. GHSA-2r63-vmw6-3m3c. A crafted directory name could make the zsh shell integration send arbitrary escape sequences, such as silently replacing the clipboard via OSC 52. bash was affected in a more limited way. This only requires cd-ing into a directory from untrusted content, such as a cloned repository. macOS: GHSA-cw69-wm67-5pv8. Cmd-clicking a crafted OSC 8 hyperlink could open unsafe local files or custom URL schemes, leading to arbitrary command execution. Ghostty now blocks unsafe targets and confirms custom URL schemes. This requires user interaction (cmd-click) to trigger. macOS: GHSA-mfw9-xcr3-7gfp. The same issue as above for links detected by the link configuration, including the default URL matcher. This requires user interaction (cmd-click) to trigger. macOS: GHSA-v8cw-fg4j-jcc4. Drag-and-drop text skipped paste protection, with the same impact as above. This requires user interaction (drag-and-drop) to trigger. macOS: GHSA-mxqx-236q-wrv7. Opening a file whose name contains control characters could run a different command than the one shown in the confirmation dialog. This requires a crafted file on your system and confirming the dialog. Note: I requested CVEs for the above advisories weeks ago, but GitHub hasn't assigned them yet. If/when they're assigned, I will update the above with proper CVE numbers. PRs: #12999 #13069 #13393 #14413 #14414 Ghostty 1.4 supports macOS 27 (Golden Gate). Most of the work was compatibility fixes: Tabs in the titlebar (macos-titlebar-style = tabs) lay out correctly again. The native tab bar no longer draws as a solid gray bar on top of your theme. It now lets the new glass style blend with your terminal background. macos-titlebar-style = hidden no longer covers the top lines of the terminal when Reduce Transparency is on. The app icon no longer has a thin border. The Shortcuts "New Window" action no longer opens two windows when Ghostty is running without any windows. Ghostty 1.4 remains fully compatible with prior macOS versions back to and including macOS 13 (Ventura). See the system requirements for more details. Ghostty 1.3.1 works on macOS 27, but it has some of the visual issues listed above, such as the gray tab bar. PRs: #13943 #13939 #13935 #13934 #13893 #13933 #13389 #13270 #13281 Ghostty now supports Kitty graphics animation and relative placements. These were the last major features of the Kitty graphics protocol that Ghostty didn't support. Programs that display animated images with the Kitty protocol, such as an animated GIF shown with kitten icat, now animate in Ghostty instead of showing a single still frame. Frame transmission, composition, and playback control are all supported, and animations pause while the terminal isn't visible. Relative placements let a program position one image relative to another image's placement, so the child image moves along with its parent. We also did a full conformance pass against the specification and Kitty itself, fixing dozens of behavioral differences. For example, images now scroll with text inside scroll regions (#4323 ), retransmitting an image ID replaces the old image (#6711 ), and invalid image data now gets an error response instead of silence, which could leave clients hanging. The full list is in the terminal capabilities section. Kitty graphics are faster, too. Image payloads are now parsed in bulk with SIMD instead of one byte at a time, making large image transfers about 16x faster to parse in our benchmarks (64 MiB of image data, x86_64 Linux), and drawing images costs much less per frame. Our Kitty graphics implementation now covers 100% of the published specification, making Ghostty (and libghostty) the first terminal to do this outside of Kitty itself. PRs: #13264 #13473 #13240 #13245 #14130 #14137 #14138 #14017 Ghostty now transparently compresses scrollback that isn't visible, reducing the physical memory those pages use by 70% to 90% for typical text-heavy history. Compression only runs while the terminal is idle and pages are decompressed on demand when you scroll back or search, so it has no measurable impact on I/O throughput. Thanks to compression, the default scrollback limit has been raised from 10 MB to 50 MB per terminal. On platforms that support compression, a full scrollback still generally uses less physical memory than the old 10 MB limit did. Compression lowers resident (physical) memory, not virtual memory, so look at resident memory when measuring it. It is currently available on macOS and 64-bit Linux. Beyond scrollback, memory usage is lower in many places: A new, empty terminal now uses about 16 KiB of terminal page memory on macOS, down from 128 KiB in Ghostty 1.3.1. On macOS and Linux, memory freed by clearing or trimming scrollback is now returned to the OS instead of being held until the terminal closes. Hidden tabs release their GPU resources. On macOS, with one visible tab and 20 hidden tabs, GPU memory dropped from about 385 MiB to 18 MiB. Rebuilding them when a tab becomes visible again takes under a millisecond. PRs: #13209 #13220 #13226 #13227 #13537 #13827 #13587 #14011 #13722 #14035 #12760 There are performance improvements across the board in Ghostty 1.4 that yield significant gains compared to prior Ghostty versions. The biggest win came from a surprising discovery: on macOS, the kernel caps every read from a pty at about 1 KiB no matter how large the read buffer is. Previously, Ghostty processed each read as it arrived, so per-read overhead was paid every kilobyte, and the program writing output sat blocked while we parsed. Ghostty now drains the pty on one thread while parsing on another, raising end-to-end I/O throughput by 25% to 55% on macOS (M4 Max, plain and Unicode text) over Ghostty 1.3.x. VT processing itself is also much faster. In parser benchmarks, plain ASCII text went from 128 MB/s to 725 MB/s (5.7x), CJK text got 3.4x faster, and a 2.6 GB dataset of real-world terminal recordings from asciinema is processed about 25% faster. Together, these changes took cat-ing a 150 MB text file on macOS from 1.5 seconds to 566 milliseconds. Other notable improvements: Resize: resizing a terminal with a large scrollback is about 6x faster (120x80 with 10,000 lines of scrollback), and 3x to 5x faster with history full of CJK text or emoji. Rendering: the renderer holds the terminal lock 2.7x to 11x less per frame, leaving more time for the I/O thread during heavy output. Copy and search: formatting terminal contents as plain text, HTML, or VT, which backs clipboard copy, write_screen_file, and scrollback search, is 1.5x to 8x faster. Launch (macOS): about 15% faster from launch to visible window, and 27% faster to the first rendered frame. Idle energy: on macOS, the renderer's display link now sleeps when there's nothing to draw. On GTK, hidden tabs stop rendering, matching macOS. Large OSC sequences: OSC 52 clipboard payloads parse about 30x faster, and even short sequences like title changes are about 6x faster. PRs: #14052 #14269 The GTK app has a new rendering pipeline. It no longer uses GtkGLArea. Instead, the renderer draws with EGL on its own thread, exports each frame as a DMABUF, and hands it to GTK to display. Rendering is now triple-buffered, which should greatly reduce tearing, and no OpenGL calls run on the main thread anymore, which let us remove a number of workarounds. The most visible result is crisp text under fractional scaling. Text and box-drawing characters are no longer blurry with fractional display scaling such as 125% or 150% (#1938 ). We fixed this once before, but it came back after upstream GTK changes. Ghostty now renders at the window's true fractional scale, so every rendered pixel maps to exactly one pixel on screen. The new render surface needs a system EGL library (see Changes for Package Maintainers). On GPU drivers that can't export DMABUFs, Ghostty falls back to copying frames through the CPU, which is slower but works. PRs: #13962 #13993 #13995 #13998 #14002 #14061 Ghostty now implements the Kitty clipboard protocol (OSC 5522) on both macOS and GTK. Ghostty 1.3 could parse the protocol but didn't implement it. OSC 52 can only read and write plain text. The Kitty clipboard protocol lets programs running in the terminal read and write any kind of clipboard data, such as images or HTML, and lets them pick among the formats on the clipboard. Programs can also enable paste events (mode 5522), which tell the program what formats a paste contains so it can read the one it wants. This is how a terminal program can accept a pasted image, for example. Clipboard access follows the existing clipboard-read and clipboard-write configurations. By default, reads prompt for permission and writes are allowed. The permission prompt shows a preview of the clipboard contents, including images. Programs that send a password can have your answer remembered for the rest of that terminal session. A new clipboard-write-limit-bytes configuration limits the size of a single write (default 64 MiB). A write over the limit fails and leaves the clipboard untouched. PRs: #10423 #13706 You can now rearrange splits on GTK by dragging them, matching the macOS feature introduced in Ghostty 1.3. When a tab has two or more splits, each split shows a drag handle at the top. Grab the handle and drop the split onto any other split, including splits in other tabs and windows. An overlay shows which side of the target split it will land on. The terminal contents, working directory, and running processes all move with it. A new drag-handle configuration controls when drag handles are shown on both macOS and GTK: auto (default), always, or never. With never, splits can't be rearranged with the mouse. Hiding the handles was a common request from users who found them in the way. On GTK, splits can only be dropped onto other splits. Dragging a split out to create a new tab or window is macOS-only. PRs: #14454 #13494 #14483 #14538 #14673 #14375 #14144 Ghostty 1.4 includes dozens of improvements to core terminal emulation. We now run esctest, Thomas Dickey's terminal conformance suite, against Ghostty's terminal core in CI. Alongside that, we fixed many differences from xterm in cursor movement within margins, tab stops, character sets, mode reports, and more. You can find the full list of related changes in the terminal capabilities section. Ghostty also supports several new sequences, including soft terminal reset (DECSTR), extended cursor position reports (DECXCPR), backarrow key mode (DECBKM), and screen size reports in characters (CSI 19 t). Programs can also now ask whether the terminal is visible using visibility reports (mode 2033), so they can stop rendering while hidden. Keyboard encoding also matches xterm more closely, with fixes for modifyOtherKeys mode 2 and legacy Alt-as-Escape encoding of non-ASCII keys. Two new sequences are disabled by default because they can be abused by untrusted programs, including ones running on a remote machine: # Allow programs to resize the window (CSI 8 t) vt-window-resize-allowed = true # Allow programs to request screen checksums (DECRQCRA) vt-xt-checksum-report = true PRs: #12582 #12814 #13533 #13844 #14472 #14854 Ghostty 1.2 introduced SSH shell integration features as a work in progress. In Ghostty 1.4, they're backed by a new ghostty +ssh CLI action: a drop-in ssh wrapper that prepares the remote session for Ghostty and then runs the real ssh with your arguments forwarded unchanged. ghostty +ssh user@example.com # Or alias it so every ssh invocation goes through it alias ssh='ghostty +ssh --' Before connecting, +ssh installs Ghostty's terminfo on the remote host so the proper xterm-ghostty TERM value can be used, and forwards COLORTERM, TERM_PROGRAM, and TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION. If the terminfo install fails (for example, tic isn't available on the remote), it falls back to TERM=xterm-256color. Flags such as --terminfo=false, --forward-env=false, and --verbose control each step. The ssh-env and ssh-terminfo shell integration features (still opt-in) now call +ssh too. Previously, each shell integration carried its own copy of this logic, which made up roughly a third of our shell integration scripts. Now bash, zsh, fish, elvish, and Nushell all behave identically, and you can get the same behavior from scripts or anywhere else by calling ghostty +ssh directly. The terminfo install itself is also more reliable. Ghostty now always installs its own bundled terminfo rather than accepting whatever xterm-ghostty entry the remote already has, and it reinstalls automatically when a Ghostty update changes the terminfo. It also no longer needs infocmp or Ghostty's terminfo on the local machine. Installs are cached per host and port, so two machines behind one address no longer share a cache entry. And ssh-env no longer silently overrides SetEnv entries in your ~/.ssh/config (#11518 ). The +ssh-cache command that manages this cache now takes positional destinations (ghostty +ssh-cache user@example.com) and has a new --prune=30d flag. See the breaking changes if you script against +ssh-cache. macOS: The minimum required macOS version for Ghostty 1.4 remains unchanged (macOS 13 Ventura). Ghostty is now compatible with macOS 27. GTK: Ghostty 1.4 requires GTK 4.18 and libadwaita 1.7, up from GTK 4.14 and libadwaita 1.5 in Ghostty 1.3. This aligns with our GTK/Adwaita version policy. Notably, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS doesn't meet this requirement. Systems with older GTK or Adwaita versions can work around this requirement by using an older version of Ghostty or the Flatpak package. #14330 OpenGL (GTK): The minimum required OpenGL version remains 4.3, but Ghostty now renders through EGL instead of GTK's OpenGL widget. This should be invisible for nearly everyone, but if Ghostty fails to start with an EGL error, please make sure your GPU driver provides a working EGL implementation. We previously announced that Ghostty 1.4 would require macOS 14. Nothing forced our hand to do this in this release, so we kept macOS 13 support. We still plan to drop macOS 13 in a future release. Apple dropped security support for macOS 13 in the fall of 2025, so we recommend upgrading regardless. The following behaviors have changed in 1.4.0: copy-on-select has been reworked and now accepts none, primary, clipboard, or both. The meaning of clipboard has changed: it previously copied to both the selection clipboard and the system clipboard, and now copies only to the system clipboard. If you set copy-on-select = clipboard and want the old behavior, change it to both. #12600 #12604 macOS: copy-on-select now defaults to none (previously true), so selecting text no longer copies it anywhere and middle-click paste of the selection no longer works by default. To restore the 1.3 behavior, set copy-on-select = primary. Note that an explicit copy-on-select = true on macOS now copies selections to the system clipboard, which is different from 1.3. #12600 #12604 macOS: cmd+arrow_up and cmd+arrow_down now run jump_to_prompt again, matching Terminal.app and Ghostty 1.2. In 1.3, these keys were hardcoded to scroll to the top and bottom and couldn't be rebound. To keep the 1.3 behavior, set keybind = cmd+arrow_up=scroll_to_top and keybind = cmd+arrow_down=scroll_to_bottom. #12245 GTK: The default ctrl+shift+page_up and ctrl+shift+page_down keybinds now move the current tab left and right (move_tab), matching Firefox, GNOME Terminal, and VS Code. jump_to_prompt moved to ctrl+shift+arrow_up and ctrl+shift+arrow_down, so programs running in the terminal no longer receive those keys. If a program you use needs them, unbind them with keybind = ctrl+shift+arrow_up=unbind and keybind = ctrl+shift+arrow_down=unbind. #4998 #12458 The list below contains deprecations that remain compatible today through a compatibility layer, but may break in a future release if they are ignored: scrollback-limit has been renamed to scrollback-limit-bytes, to make room for the new scrollback-limit-lines. #13473 copy-on-select = true is replaced with copy-on-select = primary on Linux and FreeBSD, or copy-on-select = clipboard on macOS. copy-on-select = false is replaced with copy-on-select = none. #12600 #12604 There is no set timeline to remove these deprecations, but we recommend adapting to the new configurations sooner rather than later to avoid any possible disruptions in the future. Scrollback history is now transparently compressed while the terminal is idle, reducing the physical memory used by compressed scrollback by 70% to 90% for typical text. Compression is available on macOS and 64-bit Linux and can be disabled with the new scrollback-compression configuration. Because of this, the default scrollback limit has been raised from 10 MB to 50 MB, which on average still uses less memory than a full scrollback did previously. #13264 A new configuration scrollback-limit-lines limits scrollback by number of lines instead of bytes. The existing scrollback-limit configuration has been renamed to scrollback-limit-bytes (the old name continues to work). If both are set, the first limit reached applies, and both accept unlimited. #13473 copy-on-select now accepts none, primary, clipboard, and both and no longer affects middle-click paste (see middle-click-action). clipboard now copies only to the system clipboard, so use both for the previous behavior. The default on macOS is now none. See the breaking changes for migration details. #12600 A new configuration middle-click-action configures the behavior of middle-clicking: primary-paste (default) pastes from the selection clipboard, clipboard-paste pastes from the system clipboard, and ignore does nothing. #12478 A new binding action move_tab_to_new_window moves the current tab into a new window of its own. It is also available in the command palette. #2630 A new CLI command +explain-config prints the documentation for a configuration option or binding action, e.g. ghostty +explain-config font-size. #11546 The +explain-config and +show-config CLI commands now page their output through $GHOSTTY_PAGER or $PAGER (falling back to less) when run interactively. Paging can be disabled with --no-pager or by setting the pager to an empty value. #11940 A new configuration drag-handle controls when the split drag handles are shown: auto (default), always, or never. #13706 #13709 Scrollback search now wraps around when navigating past the first or last match. #11449 A new configuration link-osc8 (default true) can be set to false to disable OSC 8 hyperlinks entirely. Disabled OSC 8 hyperlinks are not highlighted, previewed, copied, or opened. #13634 Processes running in Ghostty now receive a GHOSTTY_SURFACE_ID environment variable that uniquely identifies the terminal they are running in. #12027 The right-click context menu now has a "Close Split" item. #11173 #11174 Upgrade to Unicode 18. #14293 I/O throughput is 25% to 55% higher on macOS by reading from the pty concurrently with parsing previously read output. #13209 VT processing is significantly faster across the board. But a large part of the 1.4 development cycle went into libghostty, so here's an update. Over the past 6 months, the C API for libghostty-vt has grown from a parser and a few encoders into a complete terminal emulator API, adopted by dozens of free and commercial terminal emulators used by millions of people. It's hard to quantify exactly, but the number of people using a libghostty-based terminal is confidently several times the number of people using the Ghostty GUI. libghostty-vt now builds for macOS, Linux, Windows (MSVC and GNU), FreeBSD, Android, iOS, and WebAssembly, and CI continuously verifies every one of these targets. The goal is for libghostty-vt to be generally usable everywhere, within reason, so if you want more target support, let us know! It's also easier to integrate libghostty-vt into existing build systems. There's CMake support, Nix packaging, an xcframework, and a source tarball, in addition to the existing pkg-config file. libghostty-vt no longer needs libc++, and it can build freestanding. The API is still marked as a work in progress and broke compatibility several times during this cycle, so expect more breaking changes before a tagged release. The API documentation and the Zig, C, C++, Swift, and WebAssembly examples (now over 30) are kept up to date with main. We're going to do a final pass over the C API, break ABI one more time, and then likely tag a libghostty 1.0 release very soon. Ghostty is a non-profit project, fiscally sponsored by Hack Club. All of our finances are public on HCB, so you can see exactly where every dollar goes. During the 1.4 cycle, we paid $41,820 to contributors under contract and spent about $1,260 on infrastructure such as website hosting. I'm happy to share that we've now signed our first two 12-month contracts, which give contributors stable, long-term paid work on Ghostty and help ensure the ongoing stability and sustainability of the project: @trag1c is Ghostty's head of operations. He manages the community on GitHub and Discord, coordinates our volunteer translators, and maintains various other important project systems. @vancluever works on various Ghostty subsystems. In this cycle, he led the upgrade to Zig 0.16, moved the build off Zig's deprecated @cImport, updated the bundled Fontconfig, and more. He's also the author of z2d, the 2D graphics library Ghostty uses to draw box-drawing characters and other sprite glyphs. If you'd like to support Ghostty, please visit our sponsorship page. The primary focus of the roadmap continues to be libghostty functionality, stability, and portability. During the last release cycle, I said I aimed to tag a libghostty release. We haven't done that yet, but I'm confident we will do so before Ghostty 1.5. libghostty is a project that continues to be the tide that lifts all boats. libghostty improvements tie directly to Ghostty GUI improvements as well as dozens of other large projects in the ecosystem. As more large projects adopt libghostty, libghostty tends to get more testing and attention, and this creates a cycle that yields the most gain for terminal emulators everywhere. macOS and GTK builds of Ghostty have talented, capable maintainer teams that are continuing to improve them, so they're not neglected by any means! As a project, we've decided to drop any roadmap for Windows support in the Ghostty GUI. libghostty fully supports Windows (and we test it in CI), and the official stance now is that downstream projects should use that. Our release cycle remains 6 months. This release was delayed by one month, but Ghostty 1.5 is planned for March 2027. libghostty will have a separate release cycle.

blocks.html_en: Over the past 6 months, the C API for libghostty-vt has grown from a parser and a few encoders into a complete terminal emulator API, adopted by dozens of free and commercial terminal emulators used by millions of people. It's hard to quantify exactly, but the number of people using a libghostty-based terminal is confidently several times the number of people using the Ghostty GUI.
